Fun fact for today’s edit: a lot of people see tigers and automatically assume they aren’t that good at camouflage. Bright orange doesn’t blend in very well with vibrant greens of their tropical forest right? And definitely not well with the stark snowy white for some tigers. Well, that’s what we humans see, but for the eyes of a tigers prey, which are usually small hoofed mammals like antelope or wild boars, they have dichromatic eyes, meaning they cannot see red hues, which includes orange. So a bright orange tiger that people think to be very conspicuous and not sneaky at all, is almost invisible in a green jungle. Orange and red colors become green to the eyes of a tigers prey, allowing the tiger to easily sneak up undetected, and a tigers black stripes only benefit the camouflage even further. My favorite feature of a tiger is the cute white dots on the back of their ears, which act as a second pair of eyes, not meaning they can see out of those spots, but that they look like a pair of eyes which can deter predators from attacking because in the wild, when a predator is detected by its soon to be food, it usually leaves since the element of surprise isn’t in their favor. - #tiger #animals #edit #fyp #fypシ゚viral @lay ᢉ𐭩 @𓂃⟡ ݁꒰kyky ( ˶ˆᗜˆ˵ )꒱ ⸝⸝  .ᐟ . @danny🐟 @?🧩 @ana @🦌
